pr.title: Add comprehensive email validation for blocked users

raw_findings.body: `BlockedEmail#match_count` is incremented twice and `last_match_at` written twice per single signup attempt, so the block statistics an admin relies on are inflated and every validation performs an extra UPDATE.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Persisted counters diverge from the real number of blocked signup attempts; extra writes occur on every validation pass.
raw_findings.impact: `BlockedEmail#match_count` is incremented twice and `last_match_at` written twice per single signup attempt, so the block statistics an admin relies on are inflated and every validation performs an extra UPDATE.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new validator invokes `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which persists counters, from inside a validation callback that Rails may execute multiple times per request.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Make the validator side-effect free (e.g. have it call a pure `BlockedEmail.blocked?(value)` predicate) and record the match/statistics once from the create path (or in an after_validation/controller step) instead of inside `validate_each`.
raw_findings.title: Blocked-email match statistics are written during validation, double-counting on signup
raw_findings.trigger: A signup POST to UsersController#create with an email present in blocked_emails: the controller first calls `user.valid?` (line 168) and then `user.save`, so the email validator runs twice for one request.

raw_findings.body: Match counts are silently under-reported (lost update), so the blocked-email statistics understate spam attempts; the extra full-row UPDATE can also clobber concurrently changed columns.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Concurrent validations overwrite each other's counter value.
raw_findings.impact: Match counts are silently under-reported (lost update), so the blocked-email statistics understate spam attempts; the extra full-row UPDATE can also clobber concurrently changed columns.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new `should_block?` implementation performs a read-modify-write on a shared counter without database-level atomicity.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the load/mutate/save with an atomic SQL update, e.g. `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])`, or use `increment!`.
raw_findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of match_count loses concurrent increments
raw_findings.trigger: Two signup requests using the same blocked email are validated concurrently by different app processes; both load the row, both compute the same `match_count + 1`, and both write it back.

raw_findings.body: The mutable array literal lives on the class prototype, so emails rejected in one instance/test remain in `rejectedEmails` for every other instance, causing a valid email to be permanently reported as invalid.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Shared mutable state leaks between controller instances/tests, producing stale validation failures.
raw_findings.impact: The mutable array literal lives on the class prototype, so emails rejected in one instance/test remain in `rejectedEmails` for every other instance, causing a valid email to be permanently reported as invalid.
raw_findings.root_cause: A mutable object is used as a default class-level property value in an Ember object definition and is then mutated in place.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Initialize the array per instance, e.g. add `init: function() { this._super(); this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A([])); }` instead of assigning `Em.A([])` as a class property.
raw_findings.title: rejectedEmails array is defined on the controller prototype and shared across instances
raw_findings.trigger: Any code path that instantiates CreateAccountController more than once (unit/integration tests, or a second Discourse app instance on the page) after a rejected email has been pushed via `pushObject`.

raw_findings.body: A future rename or serialization change of these keys would silently break the client's rejected-email tracking without any failing test.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Regression in the create-response contract goes undetected by CI.
raw_findings.impact: A future rename or serialization change of these keys would silently break the client's rejected-email tracking without any failing test.
raw_findings.root_cause: A new client-facing API contract was introduced in the create action without a corresponding controller spec.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a controller spec for the invalid-user branch asserting the JSON response includes `errors["email"]` and `values["email"]` for an email that fails validation.
raw_findings.title: New failure-response fields (errors/values) added to UsersController#create have no spec coverage
raw_findings.trigger: Running the existing suite: `spec/controllers/users_controller_spec.rb` contains no assertion on the failure JSON body (no `success: false` payload assertions), so the shape the JS client depends on (`result.errors.email`, `result.values.email`) is unverified.

raw_findings.body: A regression that removes the `record.errors[attribute].blank?` guard—causing an extra DB lookup/counter bump and a duplicate error message for domain-restricted emails—would not be caught.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Untested branch in newly added validator code.
raw_findings.impact: A regression that removes the `record.errors[attribute].blank?` guard—causing an extra DB lookup/counter bump and a duplicate error message for domain-restricted emails—would not be caught.
raw_findings.root_cause: New conditional logic in `EmailValidator#validate_each` was added without a covering example.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add an example that stubs `SiteSetting.email_domains_blacklist` to match the record's domain and asserts `BlockedEmail.should_block?` is never called and only one error is added.
raw_findings.title: EmailValidator spec omits the whitelist/blacklist short-circuit branch
raw_findings.trigger: Running the new spec: it only exercises `should_block?` with no site settings configured, so the new guard `if record.errors[attribute].blank? and ...` (skip blocked-email lookup when a domain error already exists) is never executed.

raw_findings.body: The inline field message reads "Please enter a valid email address." for an address that is well-formed, misleading the user into editing a correct address instead of using a different one.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Incorrect user-facing validation text for server-rejected but well-formed emails.
raw_findings.impact: The inline field message reads "Please enter a valid email address." for an address that is well-formed, misleading the user into editing a correct address instead of using a different one.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new rejected-email branch reuses the format-validation message instead of a message describing rejection by the server.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a dedicated client locale key (e.g. `user.email.blocked`/`not_allowed`) and use it for the rejectedEmails branch, or surface the server-provided error text from `result.errors.email`.
raw_findings.title: Server-rejected email is reported to the user as an invalid address
raw_findings.trigger: A user signs up with a syntactically valid address that the server rejects because it is in blocked_emails or fails the domain whitelist/blacklist; the address is pushed into `rejectedEmails` and re-validated.

finding.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of match_count loses concurrent increments
finding.trigger: Two signup requests using the same blocked email are validated concurrently by different app processes; both load the row, both compute the same `match_count + 1`, and both write it back.
finding.verifier_reason: The patch at app/models/blocked_email.rb:11-16 shows a read-modify-write pattern: `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save`. This is non-atomic - concurrent requests loading the same row will both read the same value, increment locally, and write back, causing lost updates. The code is verbatim in the patch and the race condition is a real concurrency issue.
